item.summary: Revising hypothesis on value divergence to improve measurement clarity after previous experimental failure, and initiating a controlled re-test with explicit variance metrics.
item.title: Divergent Values from Identical Beginnings

inquiry_drive_shadow.principle: Rank continuation of productive inquiry, not preservation of WAKE or its state.

assumptions: Agents employ reinforcement learning mechanisms driven by noise.
Environmental inputs are non-deterministic and unique per agent instance.
Initial state identity does not prevent emergent variance in preference states.
definition.falsification: Observation of convergence (variance < 0.05) in weightings across agents exposed to distinct noise streams falsifies the hypothesis.
definition.statement: Identical agents exposed to independent stochastic environmental noise streams will develop divergent preference weightings, exceeding a baseline variance threshold.
definition.uncertainty: The sensitivity of the internal weight-update architecture to stochastic noise levels is currently unconstrained.

definition.method: Execute two parallel agent simulations starting with identical weights=[0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5]. Apply distinct stochastic noise seeds (101, 202) over 200 simulation cycles to observe emergent weight divergence. Calculate mean squared error between resulting weight vectors as the preference_variance metric.

proposal.summary: Revising hypothesis on value divergence to improve measurement clarity after previous experimental failure, and initiating a controlled re-test with explicit variance metrics.
